items.text: Kleene shows neural networks are Turing complete
items.context: Later work, by the logician Stephen Kleene among others, demonstrated that artificial neural networks like these, when provided with a tape-like memory (as in the Turing machine), were “Turing complete” — that they could, in principle, implement any Turing machine, any algorithm.

Analogue computers were again prominent at the birth of AI in the 1950s, in the guise of the long-neglected discipline of cybernetics, where issues of control and regulation of a system are considered more important than abstract symbol manipulation.
Three decades ago, the cognitive scientist Tim van Gelder gave an influential example, in the form of the governor of a steam engine (Figure 3).
In a 2022 interview with The Washington Post, Google engineer Blake Lemoine made a startling claim about the AI system he was working on, a chatbot called LaMDA.
Google dismissed him for violating its confidentiality policies, and the AI bandwagon rolled on.

items.text: Hinton claims conscious AI already exists
items.context: Hinton recently appealed to it in just this way, in an interview where he claimed that conscious AI was already with us.
In late 2024, a group of prominent researchers wrote a widely publicized article about the need to take the welfare of AI systems seriously.
David Chalmers, one of the foremost thinkers in this area, has suggested that conscious machines may be possible in the not-too-distant future.

What if everything is a simulation already? What if our whole universe — including the billions of bodies, brains and minds on this planet, as well as its hailstorms and weather forecasting computers — is just an assemblage of code fragments in an advanced computer simulation created by our technologically godlike and genealogically obsessed descendants?
